full_judgment:
Mr. Md. Ruhul Quddus, J.:- This Rule, at the instance of a legal heir of a judgment debtor in a mortgage decree, was issued calling in question the proceeding in Execution Case No. 727 of 2005 of Artha Rin Adalat No. 4, Dhaka and the legality of order dated 7.8.2007 passed therein rejecting an application for release of the auctioned property on paument of the decretal money. 

 2. Facts leading to this writ petition, in short, are that the Islami Bank Ltd, Mirpur, Branch, Dhaka as plaintiff instituted Artha Rin Suit No.777 of 2004 in. Artha Rin Adalat No.4, Dhaka for recovery of loan amounting, to Taka 6, 69,706/= (six lac sixty-nine thousand seven hundred six) only against the petitioner's parents Tannur Ali and Nasira Bibi. The suit was ultimately decreed ex-parte on 22.3.2005 (decree signed on 29 3.2005) giving 60 (sixty) days-time to the judgment debtors to pay the decretal amount in favour of the decree holder-bank. As the judgment debtors failed to pay the decretal amount, the bank put the decree in execution by filing Artha Jail Case No.727 of 2005 on 27.10.2005. In course of proceedings in the said execution case, the mortgaged property was put in auction on 31.7.2006 and the highest bid of Taka 7,70,000/= (seven lac seventy thousand) only was accepted 

 3. The petitioner's father being a judgment debtor came to learn about the auction sale and filed Miscellaneous Case No 29 of 2007 for setting aside the ex-parte decree depositing 10% of the decretal amount, but it was dismissed. Being aggrieved by the said order of dismissal, he preferred Artha Rin Appeal No.4 of 2007 depositing 40% of the decretal amount. The learned Judge of the appellate Court heard the appeal and dismissed the same by his judgment and order dated 23.5.2007. Thereafter the judgment debtor (petitioner's father) filed an application on 9.7.2007 before the executing Court for depositing the remaining decreta amount and release the property.. The executing Court, upon the said application, directed him to deposit Taka 2;00,000/. (Taka two lac) only and deferred hearing of the application on 13.7.2007. On the next date (15.7.2007) the judgment debtor filed another application for depositing remaining portion of the decretal amount, which the executing Court allowed and fixed 7.8.2007 for hearing of the application. In pursuance of the said order dated 15.7.2007, the judgment debtor deposited Taka 1,35,000/= (one lac thirty-five thousand) only as the remaining portion of the decretal amount, and that he deposited the entire decretal amount. The learned Judge of the executing Court ultimately heard the application and rejected it by order dated 7.8.2007. 

 5. The added respondent Nos.5-7 have appeared and contested the Rule by filing an affidavit-in-opposition contending inter alia, that the execution case was filed well within time; that the auction was held on 31.7.2006 i.e long before passing of the impugned order on 7.8.2007; that the auction purchaser had taken possession over the auctioned property and the execution case was disposed of on 18.2.2009; that subsequently the auction purchaser transferred the same to these respondents on 14.10.2009; that the petitioner obtained the instant Rule and order of statuesque suppressing the material facts. 

 6. Mr. Md. Hamm- Rashid, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner has supported the Rule and submitted that section 28 (1) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 provides special limitation of 180 days for filing an execution case, from the date of passing the executable decree. In the present case decree, was passed on 22.3,2005 and execution case was filed on 27.10.2005 i.e after expiry of 180 days and as such it is hopelessly bared by limitation. The auction held in an illegal execution proceeding is also illegal and it did not create any right and title over the mortgaged property in favour of the auction purchaser. Since the mortgaged property is the only homestead of the judgment debtor, the executing Court ought to have accepted his application and released the property. Moreover the executing Court allowed the judgment debtor to- deposit the entire decretal amount, but ultimately rejected his application for release of the mortgaged property by the impugned order and thereby sat over its own judgment, which it cannot do. In support, the learned Advocate cited the case of Khorihed Alam —Vs- Sub Ordinate Judge, Artha Rin Adalat  No. 1 and others, reported in 54 DLR, 239. 

 7. On the other hand, Mr. Joynul Abedin, the learned Advocate appearing for added respondent Nos.5-7, submits that the execution case in question is well within time in view of section 29 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, which provides that the  limitation for filing an execution case would  not run during the time given in a decree. In  present case the decree was passed with  a direction upon the judgment debtors to pay  the decretal amount in favour of the decree holder-bank within 60 (sixty) days and therefore the limitation would run after expiry of 60 (sixty) days from signing the decree on 29.3.2005. 

 10. In 54 DLR, 239 an executing Court had accepted negotiated auction price on an application filed by the decree holder-bank in an execution case under the Artha Rin Adalat Ain. Subsequently the executing Court set aside its previous order of acceptance of the negotiated price, challenging which the auction purchaser obtained Rule in a writ petition. After hearing of the Rule, the High Court Division made it absolute in part on the ground among others that "the some Court cannot sit over its own judgment in the facts of the present case." The facts and circumstances in the present case are quite different, and there is no such order by which the executing Court has set aside any of its previous orders passed in the present execution case. Therefore the case cited by the learned Advocate is distinguishable. 

 11. It appears from the decree passed in Artha Rin Suit No.777 of 2004 that it was signed on 29.3.2005 giving 60 (sixty) days-time to the judgment debtors to pay off the decretal amount in favour of the decree holder-bank (vide annexe: A-2 to the writ petition). In view of section 29 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, limitation of filing the application for execution of the decree in the present case, would run after expiry of 60 (sixty) days from 29.3.2005. Admittedly the present execution case was filed on 27.10.2005 and on calculation of limitation it appears to have been filed within 180 days after expiry of 60 (sixty) days from passing the decree. Therefore we do not find any substance in the submission of the learned Advocate for the petitioner on limitation. 

 12. It further appears from the order sheet of the execution case in question (vide annexes: H and I to the application for injunction) that after observance of all necessary legal formalities the auction was held on 31.7.2006 and the highest bid of Tulsa 7, 70,000/= quoted by respondent No.4 was accepted; respondent No.4 paid the full consideration to the executing Court on 9.8.2006; the sale was confirmed on 3.9.2006, sale certificate (boinama) was issued on 27.11.2006 and it was registered on 30.11.2006; after long laps of time, the judgment debtor (petitioner's father) filed an unusual application on 9.7.2007 for release of the auctioned property on payment of the remaining decretal amount; the learned Judge of the executing Court* though allowed him to deposit the remaining decretal amount, but ultimately rejected his application by the impugned order dated 7.82007 on the ground that there is no scope in law to redeem the property at this stage (vide annexe-G to the writ petition). 

 13. It also appears from the said order sheet that the writ of possession was returned to the executing Court on 9.9.2007. As the decree was fully satisfied with delivery of possession,. the decree holder-bank or the auction purchaser did not take any interest to pursue the execution case, as a result it was rejected for default on 18.2.2009. Thereafter the judgment debtor filed another similar application on 25.2.2008, which was also rejected by order dated 18.3,2009. Meanwhile the auction purchaser sold the property in question to added respondents No.5-7 on 14.10.2009, who mutated the record in their names and paid rent to the land office (vide annexes:3 and 3-I to the affidavit-in-opposition). As the present writ petitioner has stepped into the shoe of his father, there is no scope for him to take the plea that he was not aware of the subsequent development of the execution proceedings. Moreover the facts subsequent to order dated 7.8.2007 have been suppressed in the writ petition. In the instant Rule the proceedings of an execution case has been challenged, which is already disposed of. The judgment debtor did not file any Civil Revision under section 42 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain challenging the judgment and order dated 23.5.2007 passed in Artha Rin Appeal No.4 of 2007. During enforcement of the said judgment and order there is no scope in law to establish the fact that he had no knowledge of the Artha Rin Suit. 

 15. Before parting with the case we put it on records that the learned Judge of the executing Court allowed the judgment debtor to deposit the decretal amount beyond the scope of law and created a false hope in his mind that he may get back his property. Such an illegal order of the executing Court would not create any right for redemption of the mortgaged property in favour of the judgment debtor. This is a well settled principle of law that after confirmation of sale of any mortgaged property in due process of law, the mortgagor loses his all rights and interest over the property.
